lede: There is no dividing by a matrix. What there is instead is an inverse: the matrix that undoes what the first one did, leaving everything where it started. For a two by two there is a short formula, it is not on your formula sheet, and the whole of it is three actions.
can: Work out the determinant of a two by two matrix, sign and all
Say when a matrix has no inverse, and name the matrix that does not
Build an inverse by swapping, negating and dividing, then check it

text: The matrix that undoes the other one

md:
Multiply a number by $4$ and you undo it by multiplying by $\frac{1}{4}$. Matrices have the same idea with a different name: the **inverse** of $A$, written $A^{-1}$, is the matrix for which $A^{-1}A$ and $AA^{-1}$ both give the identity.
The identity is the matrix with ones on the leading diagonal and zeros elsewhere. It is the matrix version of $1$: multiplying by it changes nothing.

explain: Ones on the leading diagonal, zeros elsewhere: that is the identity, and reaching it is what proves the other matrix was the inverse.

text: 1. The determinant, on a line of its own

md:
Before anything else, work out the **determinant**: for $\begin{pmatrix}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{pmatrix}$ written with entries $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$, it is $ad - bc$.
Write it on its own line with its sign attached. That one habit is where this topic's marks live: the reports record slips in the arithmetic, and answers where a determinant of $-5$ became a reciprocal of $\frac{1}{5}$.

prompt: For the matrix $N = \begin{pmatrix}-3 & 2 \\ 4 & -1\end{pmatrix}$, the determinant is $ad - bc$. What is $\det N$?
explain: $(-3)(-1) - (2)(4) = -5$. Taking it the other way round would give $5$, with the sign wrong.

text: 2. When there is no inverse at all

md:
The formula divides by the determinant, so if the determinant is zero there is nothing to divide by and **no inverse exists**. A matrix like that is called **singular**.
When a question asks why an equation cannot be solved, say both halves: name the matrix, and give the reason. Examiners report answers that said the determinant was zero without making clear whose determinant it was.

prompt: A matrix has no inverse exactly when its determinant takes one particular value. What is that value?
explain: Zero. The formula divides by the determinant, and nothing can be divided by zero, so a matrix with $\det = 0$ is singular.

md:
With a determinant that is not zero, the inverse is built in three moves. **Swap** the leading diagonal, so $a$ and $d$ change places. **Negate** the other diagonal, so $b$ and $c$ change sign. **Divide** every entry by the determinant.
Do them in that order and there is nothing to remember beyond the picture below.

title: Why the formula is not on your sheet
md: The Unit 1 formula sheet gives you the quadratic formula, differentiation, integration and the logarithm definition. It gives you nothing about matrices, so this one is recall. That is why it is worth holding as a picture of three actions rather than as a line of letters.

prompt: In the three actions shown above, which pair of entries changes sign?
explain: The leading diagonal $a$ and $d$ swap places and keep their signs; $b$ and $c$ stay where they are and change sign.

text: 4. A worked inverse, and the check

md:
Find $A^{-1}$ for $A = \begin{pmatrix}4 & 1 \\ 3 & 2\end{pmatrix}$.
**Step 1.** $\det A = (4)(2) - (1)(3) = 5$.
**Step 2.** Swap and negate: $\begin{pmatrix}2 & -1 \\ -3 & 4\end{pmatrix}$.
**Step 3.** Divide by $5$: $A^{-1} = \frac{1}{5}\begin{pmatrix}2 & -1 \\ -3 & 4\end{pmatrix}$.
**Step 4.** Check: $A^{-1}A$ gives the identity.

md: This part was very well answered. The few marks that went were signs: a determinant of $-26$ written as a reciprocal of $\frac{1}{26}$. Work the determinant out on its own line, and write the reciprocal with brackets round it.

title: Inverse of a 2x2 Matrix - Corbettmaths
why: The same three actions on several matrices. It will not tell you that CCEA gives you none of this on the formula sheet, which is the part to hold on to.

prompt: For $N = \begin{pmatrix}-3 & 2 \\ 4 & -1\end{pmatrix}$ the determinant is $-5$ and swapping and negating gives $\begin{pmatrix}-1 & -2 \\ -4 & -3\end{pmatrix}$. What is the entry in row 1, column 1 of $N^{-1}$?
explain: Dividing $-1$ by $-5$ gives $1/5$. Dividing by $5$ instead, with the minus sign dropped, would give $-1/5$.

md:
Work out a determinant as $ad - bc$, on its own line, with its sign.
Say that a matrix with a zero determinant is singular, and name it when you are asked why.
Build an inverse by swapping the leading diagonal, negating the other and dividing by the determinant.
Keep the reciprocal of a negative determinant negative.
Check an inverse by multiplying back to the identity.

"Find the inverse" is a reliable $2$ marks, almost always part (i) of a longer question whose later parts depend on it. The first mark is the determinant; the second is the arranged matrix with the reciprocal attached. Stuck? Write $\det = ad - bc$ with the numbers in it. That line alone earns the first mark and tells you whether an inverse exists.
